newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Japan ADRs drop in New York trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Japan ADRs drop in New York trade.

text.p: Japanese American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) dropped in New York trade on Friday amid concerns about the strength of the Japanese economy.

The decline came after Tokyo's Nikkei 225 fell 770.22 points overnight, or 4.26 percent, to close at 17,303.65, its lowest finish since August 1995. The market reflected worries about the economy and troubled banks.

"Obviously the fundamental situation in Tokyo is not very good (and) ... eventually the fundamental problems are going to have to be met," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
A trader said Japanese stocks "are all lower. There has been some bottom fishing but the selling is still there -- it's all looking pretty grim."
Among Japanese shares, Honda Motor Co Ltd fell 2-3/8 to 91-3/8 and Toyota Motor Co was off 1-7/8 to 53-3/8 in very heavy trade.
Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd also fell 8-1/2 to 151 in very heavy trade after announcing it would focus on its semiconductor business for the next four years.
In another indicator of sliding confidence, the New York Stock Exchange's country index of Japanese stocks GXJ.N fell 1-3/4 to 28-7/8.

Among other ADRs, Nordic telecoms Nokia and AB LM Ericsson saw moderate trade after rival Motorola Inc reported better-than-expected fourth quarter earnings. Nokia rose one to 63-7/8 and Ericsson was off 7/64 to 32-1/2.
Decliners led advancers by 323 to 160 among an 807-ADR index. Volume was 41.9 million shares.
